messages:
alex: Heads up — since the 02:00 deploy we're seeing a persistent cluster of tiny GPU pods Pending in us-west2. ~120 pods, mostly 1-GPU cron jobs, and they're spread across many nodes instead of binpacking into fewer racks.
jamal: ugh. any obvious taints/affinity? scheduler logs?
alex: quick dump: nodes are fine for capacity but scheduler keeps scattering. kubectl describe shows a taint on new nodes we rolled out last week:
```
Taints: gpu-preemptable=true:NoSchedule
Labels: gpu.type=nano,gpu.count=1
```
alex: pods have no nodeSelector; they request gpu:1 and tolerations not present, so scheduler matches but still prefers spreading.
maria: are these pods setting topologySpreadConstraints or PodTopologySpread? we recently flipped default profile to minimize co-locating infra-critical pods.
alex: some do, most don't. breakdown: ~60% default batch jobs, 30% user dev jobs, 10% system tasks. node-util on affected racks shows 25-35% GPU utilization despite high pending count.
chen: this feels like two things colliding: (1) taint on new nodes is forcing tolerant pods to trickle in and (2) scheduler preference for spread to reduce single-node risk after NVLINK incidents.
jamal: can you paste a scheduler bind log snippet?
alex: log snippet: 
```
I0319 02:15:10.123 scheduler: InsufficientResources -> attempted fit, selected node with leastScore=0.2 preferSpread=true bindFailed=false
I0319 02:15:11.456 scheduler: Preemption: evaluated 3 victims, none scored lower than threshold -> placed on node X
```
maria: we recently bumped the 'podAntiAffinityWeight' in the policy to 30 to avoid noisy-neighbor GPU co-packs. That might be the culprit.
chen: short term: reduce anti-affinity weight from 30 -> 5 for the us-west2 profile, so binpack wins for 1-GPU jobs. add a policy exception for 'batch:micro' label.
alex: agree. also we should relax the taint to PreferNoSchedule or add an explicit toleration to the batch job kustomize so they co-locate when appropriate.
jamal: any cost impact yet?
alex: raw numbers: spot/instance churn up 12% since the scatter started — more nodes active for same GPU-hours. contributing to ~9% higher infra spend on GPUs last 24h.
maria: can we do a quick A/B? change scheduler profile in us-west2 to prefer binpack for pods with label `workload=micro-batch` and keep global spread for others. run for 2h and measure pending count and p95 latency.
chen: +1. I'll prepare a canary patch: update scheduler config map, keep rollout to 10% of nodes (by node selector) first.
alex: I'll add a `workload=micro-batch` label to the kustomize overlays for the pipeline jobs.
infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-1423 — "us-west2 micro-gpu fragmentation". Pagering oncall. https://infra.redwood/INC/INF-2026-1423
alex: assigning to @jamal for immediate change, @chen for config, @maria for metrics validation. I'll keep collecting traces.
jamal: on it. applying config now to canary subset. will report back in ~15m with pending delta. :running: 
maria: once canary is up, I'll publish a dashboard with: pending_count, node_gpu_util, avg_allocated_gpus_per_node, cost_delta.
chen: longer term we should:
- consolidate instance types so small `nano` SKU doesn't fragment racks
- add a scheduler plugin to prefer node-score = floor(gpu_free / job_gpu_req) to aggressively binpack small jobs
- re-evaluate taint strategy for spot smoothing vs packing
alex: sounds good. For the immediate runbook I'll add: rollback steps, expected metrics, and a link to INF-2026-1423.
jamal: canary shows pending down from 120->34 on the 10% node group after 12m. I'll keep monitoring.
alex: great. leave the canary for 2h then we can promote. thanks all :thumbsup:
